result.question:
ROBOTICS, FOUNDATION MODELS, LLMs, WORLD MODELS, WORLD-ACTION MODELS AND JEPA ARCHITECTURES — outstanding research results from JUNE 2025 to JULY 2026, and how each transfers to a hierarchical latent world model for autonomous driving. Restrict to CREDIBLE, HIGH-QUALITY sources (peer-reviewed venues, major-lab technical reports, benchmarks with public reproducible numbers). Reject hype and unreproduced claims; state evidence quality per claim.

COVER ALL OF: (1) JEPA-family — V-JEPA 2 / V-JEPA2-AC, I-JEPA successors, action-conditioned JEPA heads, latent-space prediction vs pixel reconstruction, representation-collapse controls, what JEPA has and has NOT been shown to do; (2) WORLD MODELS — Genie 3, DreamerV4 / successors, Cosmos world foundation models, video-diffusion world models, latent vs pixel rollout, LONG-HORIZON ROLLOUT STABILITY and drift, measured horizon limits; (3) WORLD-ACTION MODELS / VLAs — pi-0 / pi-0.5, GR00T N1.x, RT-2 successors, OpenVLA, latent action models (LAPO, Genie-style latent actions), action tokenisation, action chunking, flow-matching vs autoregressive action heads; (4) ROBOTICS — cross-embodiment transfer, Open-X/DROID-scale data, sim-to-real, hierarchical policies (high-level reasoner + low-level controller), failure recovery; (5) LLMs — reasoning/test-time compute, distillation into small models, hierarchical or multi-agent controllers, structured latent reasoning that could serve a STRATEGIC planner; (6) FOUNDATION MODELS generally — scaling laws for SMALL models, data quality vs quantity, curriculum, mixture-of-experts at small scale, efficient pretraining.

OUR PROGRAMME (make every recommendation concrete against this, and flag CONTRADICTIONS explicitly):
- sub-300M hierarchical 4-brain latent world model for driving (strategic / tactical / operative + fallback) over a from-scratch ViT encoder, with an action-conditioned transition predictor; deployed arm 286.3M params. Design intent is explicitly JEPA-adjacent: predict in LATENT space, not pixels.
- MEASURED: the deployed arm reaches ade_0_2s 0.4271 (881 windows / 40 eps) and 0.4108 (13,198 windows / 600 eps), both CI-separated from a constant-velocity floor, using the episode-cluster bootstrap. This is world-model FIDELITY (true future actions supplied), not planning.
- MEASURED 2026-07-29 — the key open problem: PURE IMAGINATION (camera cut after an 8-frame context, latent rollout only) degrades with a LOCAL exponent rising 1.03 -> 1.63 -> 1.87 -> 1.91 over 0.4-2.0s (ADE 0.0406 / 0.0829 / 0.1607 / 0.2753 / 0.4215); global OLS exponent 1.456. Decay ACCELERATES: near-linear early, near-quadratic by 2s. And our horizon is ARCHITECTURALLY capped at 2s by an index_select over a learned horizon embedding. WE NEED: how the best 2025-26 world models extend stable latent rollout beyond a couple of seconds, and what they measure to prove it.
- MEASURED: a FROZEN encoder (DINOv2 / I-JEPA) hit a hard ceiling on driving (2.92m fwd ADE, speed-blind); a from-scratch trained encoder with speed as an action channel fixed it (3.73 -> 0.83m, speed R2 0.61 -> 0.965). Any claim that a frozen generic video encoder suffices for driving CONTRADICTS our measurement — we want the strongest 2025-26 evidence on both sides.
- MEASURED: our scale ladder (54.7M / 104.2M / 251.9M, identical corpus, identical steps) shows the knee is ANCHOR COUNT (the trajectory-set size), NOT encoder scale. Smaller was also better for our inverse-dynamics model (0.86M > 2.90M > 19.98M). We want 2025-26 evidence on small-model scaling laws that speaks to this.
- MEASURED: substituting an ORACLE target-speed recovers 88.7% of our goal-conditioning gap, entirely longitudinal; the produced target-speed head has R2 0.7635 but RMSE 4.4545 m/s. Longitudinal intent is our single largest lever.
- CONSTRAINT: our corpus (PhysicalAI-AV) has NO map, lane graph, junction annotation, or route/goal signal, and no GNSS. A strategic brain therefore needs its topology from elsewhere (a simulator with a lane graph, or an external corpus), or from a fundamentally different formulation.

DELIVER: a structured chief-scientist report. For every finding give the claim, its evidence quality, the number, and a CONCRETE TESTABLE TRANSFER to us — which of our hypotheses it advances or falsifies, the cheapest discriminating experiment, and rough GPU cost. Rank by (expected gain / cost). Give special weight to anything that (a) extends stable latent rollout beyond 2s, (b) bears on frozen-vs-trained encoders for control, (c) gives a small model a strategic/topological prior without map labels, or (d) CONTRADICTS one of our measured results above.
result.summary: Across five verified primary sources the answer to our central question is negative and consistent: as of July 2026 NO published system demonstrates stable PURE latent rollout much beyond a couple of seconds, and the current JEPA flagship (V-JEPA 2-AC) deploys a planning horizon of 1 step (~0.25 s at 4 fps) with receding-horizon replanning precisely because "the accuracy of the representation-space predictions decreases with longer autoregressive rollouts". The field's three actual workarounds are per-step replanning, sub-goal/graph decomposition over REAL dataset states (not imagined ones), and training-time recovery from self-corrupted histories — the last of which (HorizonDrive) is the only driving-specific result with a quantitative long horizon, ~20 s, and that is in a pixel-reconstructive VAE latent scored with video metrics, not a JEPA latent. The single highest-value transfer is not an architecture change at all: SkyJEPA's compounding ratio CR_k = e_rollout / e_teacher-forced shows our headline local exponent (1.03 → 1.91 over 0.4–2.0 s) CANNOT distinguish "the task gets harder with horizon" from "our rollout compounds its own error", so our most-quoted imagination number is confounded and disambiguating it costs ~0 GPU. Our 2 s cap is also cheaper to lift than assumed — stack/tanitad/models/predictor.py already carries a k=1 head and an out_proj annotated "reserved: feed predictions back" — but lifting it without a rollout-recovery training scheme buys longer rollouts that diverge faster, not better ones. Finally, sections 3–6 of the question (VLAs/world-action models, robotics transfer, LLM reasoning, small-model scaling laws) produced ZERO surviving claims, so this report is admissible only on JEPA and world-model horizon questions and must not be cited on encoder scale, anchor count, target-speed heads, or the no-map strategic brain.

findings.claim: RANK 1 (highest gain/cost) — OUR HEADLINE IMAGINATION NUMBER IS CONFOUNDED, AND THE FIX IS FREE. SkyJEPA introduces exactly the instrument our 0.4–2.0 s exponent lacks: a compounding ratio CR_k = e_k,rollout / e_k,TF that normalises open-loop rollout error by TEACHER-FORCED error at the SAME step, plus a per-step growth term ER_k = E[e_k − e_{k−1}]. This separates 'predicting 2 s ahead is intrinsically harder than 0.4 s ahead' from 'our rollout is compounding its own error' — two hypotheses our reported local exponent rise (1.03 → 1.63 → 1.87 → 1.91; global OLS 1.456) cannot distinguish, because ADE-vs-horizon confounds both. SkyJEPA trains rollout on only T=20 steps (1.0 s at 20 Hz) yet measures drift to k=60 (3.0 s, 3x the trained horizon) and reports CR≈1.4 at k=60 vs ≈2.4 for an autoregressive predictive baseline. CONCRETE TESTABLE TRANSFER: add a teacher-forced arm to taniteval/taniteval/imagination.py and re-score the SAME 40 val episodes with both paths, reporting CR_k and ER_k at k=4/8/16/20 with the episode-cluster bootstrap from taniteval/taniteval/ci.py. PRE-REGISTERED OUTCOMES: (a) CR_k flat near 1 ⇒ the 'accelerating decay' narrative is FALSIFIED, the acceleration is task difficulty, and no architecture change is justified; (b) CR_k rising super-linearly ⇒ compounding is real, and the rollout-recovery training in RANK 3 is the indicated fix, not a bigger horizon. GPU COST: ESTIMATED 0–6 GPU-hours on one A6000 (zero if per-step teacher-forced latents are already dumped). THIS MUST RUN BEFORE ANY ARCHITECTURE CHANGE PREDICATED ON THE EXPONENT.
findings.evidence: SkyJEPA (arXiv 2606.23444, Rao/Zhang/Balestriero/LeCun/Loianno, NYU ARPL + Brown, v1 2026-06-22, 'Under Review') verified 3-0 unanimous at HIGH verifier confidence: metric definitions confirmed VERBATIM in both v1 and v2 ('CRk = (ek,rollout^x)/(ek,TF^x)', 'ERk = E[ek^x - ek-1^x]'), T=20/20 Hz and k=60 arithmetic confirmed, 1.4/2.4 confirmed verbatim, baseline confirmed autoregressive, and Fig. 6 caption confirms the confound-separation reading ('values above 1 indicate error accumulation caused by recursion'). An anti-confabulation control (non-leading prompt) returned seven metrics including unasked-for LeCun-lab signatures (temporal straightening, SO(3)-log attitude error), confirming genuine document access. Confidence is HIGH because the load-bearing element is a DEFINITION, whose validity does not depend on the source's peer-review status, and because the same distinction is independently forced by two other verified sources: MoP-JEPA's Fig. 7 x-axis is true GOAL DISTANCE not rollout step, and V-JEPA 2 states error accumulation as an author-acknowledged limitation. CAVEATS THAT MUST TRAVEL: the 1.4/2.4 figures are prose readings of a figure with the authors' own 'approximately' hedge; CR is still RISING at k=60, not asymptoting, so the claim's word 'bounded' is a mild editorialisation; the domain is quadrotor state prediction over a low-dimensional physics vector with a physics-structured prober, NOT a high-dimensional visual world model, so the METRIC DESIGN transfers and the 1.4-at-3x NUMBER does not; no public code repository was found and no third-party reproduction exists.

findings.claim: RANK 2 — THE 2 s ARCHITECTURAL CAP IS CHEAPER TO LIFT THAN ASSUMED, AND OUR OWN CODE ALREADY RESERVES THE FEEDBACK PATH. HorizonDrive's bounded rolling window is the published alternative to a fixed learned horizon index: per-step compute and memory are bounded by a context of T+K_S frames (T=11 context, K_S=10 generated chunk) 'regardless of total horizon', with sustained wall-clock 1.8 s per 10-frame chunk on a single RTX 5090 at 256x512 (5.8 s at 384x768). Against our stack this is not a redesign: stack/tanitad/models/predictor.py already has (i) a fixed-size causal window (PredictorConfig.window=6, learned self.pos over exactly that window, asserted equal), (ii) a k=1 residual head (horizons default (1,2,4)), and (iii) an unused projection annotated verbatim `self.out_proj = nn.Linear(state_dim, d)  # reserved: feed predictions back`. A rolling-window rollout is therefore: drop the oldest state, append the k=1 prediction, re-run — no retrain, no new parameters, and cost flat in horizon. CONCRETE TESTABLE TRANSFER (inference only): recursively apply the existing k=1 head past 20 steps on the deployed arm and measure ADE and CR_k out to 4 s and 6 s, i.e. 2x and 3x the trained horizon, matching SkyJEPA's 3x protocol. PRE-REGISTERED: we EXPECT divergence to worsen past 2 s because the k=1 head was trained under teacher forcing — a negative result here is informative and is the trigger for RANK 3, not a refutation of the approach. GPU COST: ESTIMATED 2–4 GPU-hours. CONTRADICTION FLAG: this removes the COMPUTE/index cap only; HorizonDrive's own thesis is that a naive rolling window is insufficient without Scheduled Rollout Recovery, so presenting the rolling window as the answer to our accelerating decay would be an overreach the source does not support.
findings.evidence: HorizonDrive (arXiv 2605.11596, 'Self-Corrective Autoregressive World Model for Long-horizon Driving Simulation', Horizon Robotics group incl. Wei Yin / Xiaoyang Guo / Qian Zhang / Weiqiang Ren, v1 2026-05-12, v2 2026-05-22) verified 2-1 at HIGH verifier confidence: quote exact and its surrounding clause asserts latency is SUSTAINED, not merely initial; T=11 / K_S=10 (and K_T=40 teacher chunk) confirmed; wall-clock confirmed and NOT cherry-picked (the unflattering 5.8 s / 1.7 FPS operating point is reported alongside). The proposition — a fixed-size sliding context bounds per-step cost independently of horizon — is near-tautological and standard in streaming video world models, so a self-descriptive architecture section plus the authors' own latency measurement is the correct evidence tier. THREE CORRECTIONS APPLIED HERE: (1) the original claim self-labelled this 'MEASURED', which is a category error under our own CLAUDE.md taxonomy where MEASURED means ours-plus-artifact-path — relabelled PUBLISHED; (2) the verbatim quote bounds per-step COMPUTE, the memory extension is one inference past the quoted sentence (true for a fixed context, but stated as inference); (3) HorizonDrive predicts in a video-VAE RECONSTRUCTION latent (temporal compression fine-tuned 4→1) scored with FID/FVD/ARE/DTW — the rolling-window mechanism is architecture-agnostic and transfers, but the paper is NOT evidence for predictive-latent rollout stability of our kind. The code facts about our own predictor are MEASURED-ours (read directly this session at predictor.py:71–122 and config.py:50–58); note flagship_v4.py:72–73 shows the head-side horizon tuples (DENSE 1..20 = 2 s dense, TACTICAL 5..50 = 5 s coarse), so the cap is on the dense/operative path specifically. Source is an unrefereed preprint; one verifier reported a public repo (github.com/zcliangyue/HorizonDrive) inside a REFUTED claim while another found none — treat code availability as UNCONFIRMED.

findings.claim: RANK 3 — NO VERIFIED 2025-26 RESULT SHOWS STABLE PURE LATENT ROLLOUT MUCH BEYOND A COUPLE OF SECONDS; THE FIELD HAS THREE WORKAROUNDS, NOT A SOLUTION. (a) V-JEPA 2 states outright that 'autoregressive prediction suffers from error accumulation: the accuracy of the representation-space predictions decreases with longer autoregressive rollouts, thereby making it more difficult to reliably plan over long horizons', and its DEPLOYED mitigation is a SHORTER horizon, not a longer one: CEM with planning horizon = 1 for ALL tasks (Table 3, same for the Cosmos comparator), executing only the first action before re-planning, each sampled action constrained to an L1 ball of radius 0.075 (~13 cm end-effector displacement); at 4 fps that horizon is ~0.25 s. (b) MoP-JEPA extends usable planning DISTANCE not by deeper rollout but by one-pass multi-modal prediction (K hard-assigned heads + context-only router) plus GRAPH SEARCH over real dataset states — it retains 0.05–0.15 success to goal distance 14 where single-output (dense) and MDN baselines hit zero by 6–8, but its x-axis is TRUE GOAL DISTANCE, not rollout step, and the model never feeds a predicted latent back into itself; no compounding-drift experiment appears anywhere in its 9 figures / 6 tables. (c) HorizonDrive's answer is a TRAINING-TIME one: recover from your own prediction-corrupted histories. TRANSFER: our 2 s cap is NOT obviously behind V-JEPA 2, and pure-imagination decay is the field's open problem, not a TanitAD defect — but this must NOT be used to argue the cap is fine (see RANK 4), and neither V-JEPA 2 nor MoP-JEPA may be cited as evidence that anything extends stable latent rollout. The indicated experiment is a rollout-recovery fine-tune (sample training contexts from the model's own rollout trajectory) from the deployed checkpoint, ~5k steps, judged on CR_k from RANK 1, ESTIMATED 0.5–1 GPU-day.
findings.evidence: Three independent primary sources converge. V-JEPA 2 (arXiv 2506.09985, Meta FAIR, 30 authors, public MIT-licensed weights) verified 2-1 at HIGH confidence with all four specifics confirmed verbatim on two independent fetches: the error-accumulation sentence, horizon=1 in Table 3 for BOTH methods across Reach/Grasp/Pick-&-Place with no >1 ablation anywhere, receding-horizon execution, and the L1-ball 0.075 (correctly attributed to the ACTION constraint, not to the L1 energy function — a conflation trap that was checked and cleared). This is evidence AGAINST the authors' own interest, the highest-credibility class from a lab report. MoP-JEPA (arXiv 2607.05238, v1 2026-07-06, unrefereed) verified 2-1 at MEDIUM confidence: the 0.05–0.15 / distance-14 / zero-by-6-8 numbers confirmed verbatim, the one-pass mechanism confirmed from the abstract, and the ABSENCE of any rollout experiment double-probed per our absence-is-not-absence rule via a full 9-figure/6-table enumeration. CORRECTION APPLIED: the original claim named the distance-14 baselines 'single-output and codebook'; they are Dense (single-output) and MDN — the codebook control lives in a different table (coverage of stochastic dynamics) as a context-free baseline. This correction STRENGTHENS the result, since MDN is the stronger multi-modal competitor. TWO QUALIFICATIONS: V-JEPA 2 does attack error accumulation at TRAINING time (a rollout loss at T=2 alongside teacher forcing), so 'their mitigation is a shorter horizon' is true of DEPLOYMENT only; and its pick-and-place is solved by a 3-sub-goal schedule (4/10/4 timesteps) with each optimisation still at horizon 1 — decomposition, not long-horizon planning, which strengthens rather than weakens the finding. Evidence class: PUBLISHED for all three; two of the three are unrefereed preprints.

findings.claim: RANK 4 — CONTRADICTION AGAINST US: THE DRIVING-SPECIFIC HORIZON SOTA IS ~20 s QUANTITATIVE, 10x OUR CAP. HorizonDrive's quantitative evaluation reaches ~20 s of genuine autoregressive rollout (student rolls out N=20 AR steps at K_S=10 on a T=11 context = 211 frames ≈ 21 s at 10 FPS), where it improves on the strongest long-horizon streaming baselines by FID −52 %, FVD −37 %, ARE −21 %, DTW −9 %. The headline 'minute-scale rollout' is demonstrated ONLY qualitatively, in Appendix G, on a self-collected dataset (~1 minute at 10 FPS, K_S=10, T=11), with no metric attached — the authors say so themselves: 'the per-clip length of ~20 s is the dataset upper bound and determines our quantitative horizon, while longer minute-scale rollouts are shown qualitatively'. So the defensible reading is 'quantitatively evaluated to ~20 s, degrading more slowly than baselines', never 'stable to 60 s'. TRANSFER AND EXPLICIT CONTRADICTION: this falsifies any comfort that our 2 s cap matches the state of the art on horizon for DRIVING specifically. It does NOT falsify our numbers, because the comparison is not like-for-like — HorizonDrive rolls out in a pixel-reconstructive VAE latent and is scored with video-generation metrics (FID/FVD/VBench) plus trajectory metrics, whereas we roll out in a predictive latent with no decoder and score ADE in metres. The MECHANISM is what transfers (scheduled rollout recovery: train on prediction-corrupted histories), not the horizon number. Cheapest discriminating experiment: RANK 1's CR_k plus RANK 2's recursive extension establish where OUR curve actually breaks before spending anything on a 20 s target.
findings.evidence: Verified 3-0 unanimous at HIGH verifier confidence against the primary source, twice, via independent fetches. The scope sentence is the AUTHORS' OWN, not the claimant's inference, and was returned in substantively identical form on both fetches; Appendix G is titled 'Minute-level autoregressive generation' and every detail of the characterisation (self-collected dataset, 10 FPS, K_S=10, T=11, figure-only, no metric) matched exactly; K_S=10 / T=11 independently confirmed in Secs. 4.3 and 5.1. Note the abstract headline IS 'minute-scale AR rollout under bounded memory' while every abstract NUMBER is nuScenes-bound to ~20 s — so the evidence-class split (20 s MEASURED-by-authors, 60 s QUALITATIVE) is exactly right and is the paper's own position. TWO REFINEMENTS, both cutting conservative: (1) 'stable to 20 s' is generous — what is measured is relative improvement over baselines plus an explicit error-accumulation analysis in Appendix D, i.e. error still GROWS within the 20 s; (2) the metrics are pixel/video-generation metrics on an AR VIDEO model, so a 20 s pixel-space rollout is not direct evidence that a 286M latent WM can hold 20 s. Confidence is MEDIUM not HIGH: single source, arXiv preprint with no venue in the comments field, 2.5 months old, no third-party replication. The claim is DEFLATIONARY (it argues the paper proves less than its headline) and rests on the paper's own scope caveat rather than on its authority, which is why the unrefereed status does not weaken it.

findings.claim: RANK 5 — WARNING THAT BEARS DIRECTLY ON OUR CLOSED-LOOP NUMBERS: AN ONLINE-REPLANNING EXECUTOR MASKS TRANSITION-MODEL ERROR. MoP-JEPA's authors concede it verbatim: 'With 10% false edges, replanning raises success from 0.40 to 1.00. Execution can therefore repair a low-precision graph online, whereas realroute measures model fidelity.' A model whose transition set is 10 % wrong scores PERFECT under an online-replanning executor. TRANSFER TO US, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: (i) any CEM/MPC/receding-horizon executor we build on top of the 4-brain — which is precisely the V-JEPA 2 recipe and the obvious next step for our closed-loop stack — will HIDE the rising local exponent rather than fix it, so closed-loop success must never be reported as world-model validation; (ii) conversely, our measured open-loop 0.45 m → closed-loop 1.69 m gap is not necessarily a pure fidelity signal either, because the closed-loop arm's executor and its 2 s replanning cadence are part of the measurement. CONCRETE TESTABLE TRANSFER: report an open-loop fidelity number (CR_k from RANK 1) and a closed-loop success number as two SEPARATE decision inputs in taniteval/taniteval/closedloop.py, and pre-register that a closed-loop improvement with flat CR_k is an EXECUTOR gain, not a world-model gain, and may not be quoted as world-model progress. GPU COST: 0 — this is a reporting-protocol change, not an experiment.
findings.evidence: Verified 2-1 at MEDIUM verifier confidence; the concession sentence and the 0.40 → 1.00 figure were confirmed VERBATIM against the primary source, and Table 4 includes execution success alongside the fidelity metric. This is an explicit authorial concession that the executor masks fidelity, i.e. evidence against the authors' own interest. Source is arXiv 2607.05238, an unrefereed preprint three weeks old at verification, self-reported and unreplicated — quotable only as 'the paper reports', evidence class PUBLISHED-but-unrefereed, never MEASURED. The verifier explicitly noted the transfer: 'an online-replanning executor would likewise mask our 1.03→1.91 rising local exponent rather than fix it'. Confidence is MEDIUM because the underlying paper carries a confirmed factual error in its associated claim (baseline naming, corrected in RANK 3), because no external corroboration was obtainable (the verifier's search budget was exhausted at 200/200), and because the absence findings rest on model-summarised HTML fetches rather than a line-by-line read.

findings.claim: RANK 6 — LATENT (NOT PIXEL) ACTION-CONDITIONED PREDICTION IS VALIDATED ON REAL HARDWARE, AND THE ACTION-CONDITIONED HEAD IS DATA-CHEAP. V-JEPA 2-AC post-trains an action-conditioned LATENT predictor on under 62 hours of DROID robot video with no reward, no task-specific training and no data from the deployment environments, then performs image-goal pick-and-place zero-shot on Franka arms in two unseen labs: Lab 1 cup 80 % / box 80 %, Lab 2 cup 80 % / box 50 % (Table 2, out of 10 trials each). Only raw video plus 7-D end-effector state (3 position, 3 orientation, 1 gripper) are used — 'unlabeled' means no reward / task-type / success metadata, so the claim's 'action-labelled' is MORE precise than the abstract, not a misread. TRANSFER: this is the strongest external support for our latent-space design intent over pixel reconstruction, and it says an action-conditioned transition head can be fitted on a very small action-labelled slice — relevant to any plan that adds a new conditioning channel (e.g. a target-speed or intent channel) without a full corpus rebuild. QUALIFICATIONS THAT BOUND THE TRANSFER, ALL VERIFIED: the sub-goals are HUMAN-PROVIDED (two sub-goal images plus the final goal, with an automatic switch after 4 timesteps), which is why pick-and-place (80 %) scores ABOVE grasp (65–70 %) — they are not nested tasks under the same protocol; planning horizon is 1 with 800 CEM samples x 10 refinements at 16 SECONDS PER ACTION, so this is NOT evidence for long-horizon latent rollout; the camera pose was hand-tuned ('we manually tried different camera positions'); the strong cells are the cup, with Grasp Box at 20–30 %; and 'unseen labs' means unseen ENVIRONMENT, not unseen embodiment, since DROID is itself Franka-plus-parallel-gripper. No metric-accuracy and no driving evidence anywhere.
findings.evidence: Verified 3-0 unanimous at HIGH verifier confidence, VERIFIED AGAINST PRIMARY SOURCE with every checkable fact matching and no contradicting source found. All four success cells reproduce Table 2 verbatim INCLUDING the weak 50 % cell, so not cherry-picked; the n=10 trials figure is stated in the paper and the claim self-flags the small n. Source quality matches claim strength: Meta FAIR technical report (Assran, Bardes, Garrido, LeCun, Rabbat, Ballas et al.), real hardware (Franka + Robotiq), weights publicly released and MIT-licensed (dl.fbaipublicfiles.com/vjepa2/vjepa2-ac-vitg.pt; torch.hub 'vjepa2_ac_vit_giant'; facebook/jepa-wms). Not peer-reviewed, but the research question explicitly admits major-lab technical reports and the primary is the arXiv paper, not the blog. arXiv shows [v1] ONLY — no revision, erratum, or retraction of the robot numbers; a V-JEPA 2.1 exists (HF hosting request Mar 2026) but supersedes the PRETRAINING checkpoints, not the 2-AC robot measurements. ONE THING THIS FINDING MUST NOT BE USED FOR: V-JEPA 2-AC FREEZES a 1M+ hour-pretrained ViT-g and post-trains only the AC predictor, i.e. it sits on the opposite side of our measured frozen-encoder ceiling. The claim asserts nothing about frozen encoders, so this is not a contradiction of it — but the transfer sentence is silent on the point and this result must not be allowed to launder a frozen-encoder recommendation (see RANK 7).

findings.claim: RANK 7 — FROZEN-vs-TRAINED ENCODERS: OUR MEASUREMENT STANDS UNCHALLENGED, BECAUSE EVERY CANDIDATE CONTRADICTION *AND* EVERY CANDIDATE CORROBORATION FAILED VERIFICATION. Seven distinct frozen-encoder claims were tested adversarially and all seven were refuted, in BOTH directions: the claim that V-JEPA 2-AC's frozen 1B ViT-g is the strongest counter-evidence to our ceiling (1-2); three claims from arXiv 2606.07687 that would have CORROBORATED our ceiling — PSNR-vs-action-R2 orthogonality (1-2), a representational ceiling on Web-DINO/SigLIP 2 with frozen action R2 −0.01/+0.05 rising only to 0.16–0.17 after full inverse-dynamics fine-tuning (0-3), and catastrophic frozen-encoder collapse under blur/noise corruption (0-3); and three claims from arXiv 2606.09311 (FF-JEPA) including an 18M task-trained encoder beating frozen DINOv2 at long horizon 91.80 % vs 61.0 % (0-3). CONSEQUENCE: absence of a verified contradiction is NOT corroboration. Our own MEASURED result (frozen DINOv2/I-JEPA 2.92 m fwd ADE, speed-blind; from-scratch encoder with speed as an action channel 3.73 → 0.83 m, speed R2 0.61 → 0.965) remains the strongest evidence in either direction that this programme possesses. THE ONE GENUINELY UNEXPLORED AXIS: V-JEPA 2-AC's frozen encoder was VIDEO/motion-pretrained on 1M+ hours, unlike DINOv2's and I-JEPA's IMAGE pretraining — nobody has run frozen-video-encoder vs from-scratch on a metric driving task. CHEAPEST DISCRIMINATING EXPERIMENT: freeze a V-JEPA 2 ViT-L, train only our predictor and heads on the canonical 2376-episode corpus at matched steps, and read ade_0_2s against the deployed 0.4271 with the paired episode-cluster bootstrap. ESTIMATED 1–2 GPU-days. PROGRAMME-LEVEL CONTRADICTION TO FLAG BEFORE SPENDING IT: even a POSITIVE result is undeployable — ViT-g is 1B params and ViT-L alone approaches our entire sub-300M budget — so this is a research probe that would require distillation to become an arm, and it should be ranked below RANKS 1–3 for that reason.
findings.evidence: This finding is primarily a statement about THIS evidence set, which is why its confidence is medium rather than low. The single surviving datum is the verified 3-0 V-JEPA 2-AC result (RANK 6), whose frozen-ViT-g design is real but whose task is tabletop manipulation with image goals and relative end-effector actions at 16 s/action and 4 fps — not metric longitudinal prediction at road speed. The attempt to promote that design choice into a contradiction of our ceiling was voted DOWN 1-2. Symmetrically, the three arXiv 2606.07687 claims that would have supported our position were voted down 1-2, 0-3 and 0-3, and all three FF-JEPA claims 0-3 — so no admissible external evidence exists on EITHER side and none of those numbers may be quoted. Under our own taxonomy the frozen-encoder position therefore rests entirely on MEASURED-ours; any report sentence implying external corroboration would be an INHERITED claim deciding a GPU-day, which CLAUDE.md rule 1 forbids. Time-sensitivity: 2606.07687 and 2606.09311 are ~2 months old and were unverifiable within this session's search budget rather than shown false — they are UNVERIFIED LEADS worth a second probe, not refuted science.
findings.vote: 1-2 on the contradiction; 0-3 / 1-2 on all six corroborating candidates

findings.claim: RANK 8 — SPECTRAL CONSTRAINT ON THE LATENT TRANSITION: PROMISING MECHANISM, WEAK EVIDENCE, WRONG DOMAIN. Koopman Dreamer constrains the deterministic latent transition to Koopman-style 2D rotation-scaling blocks with bounded spectral radius and reports, over a 64-step action-conditioned rollout initialised from a 32-step observation context with no future observations, a 23.2 % reduction in decoded OBSERVATION MSE (lower on 8 of 9 tasks) and an 89.4 % reduction in deterministic-latent MSE (lower on 9 of 9) versus DreamerV3. TRANSFER: a spectral reparameterisation of the residual transition in stack/tanitad/models/predictor.py is a small, self-contained change that directly targets multiplicative error growth, and it composes with RANK 2's recursion — but it is UNPROVEN for a visual latent and carries a stated trade-off (lowering the radius attenuates error but erases persistent task information), which for us risks destroying exactly the speed/scale magnitude signal that our speed-channel fix bought (speed R2 0.965). SEQUENCING: do NOT run this before RANK 1. If CR_k comes back flat, there is no compounding to attenuate and this experiment is unmotivated; if CR_k rises, this becomes a legitimate second lever after rollout-recovery training. Cheapest form if it survives that gate: spectral-radius reparameterisation plus a short fine-tune from the deployed checkpoint, judged on CR_k and on speed R2 jointly (both must be reported, because the mechanism predicts a trade between them). ESTIMATED 0.5–1 GPU-day.
findings.evidence: Verified 3-0 unanimous at HIGH verifier confidence for what the paper SAYS — arXiv 2607.19719, 'Koopman Dreamer: Spectrally Constrained Latent Dynamics for Stable World-Model Imagination', Li/Zhang/Xie/Lan/Pan/Xu, submitted 2026-07-22 (7 days old), cs.LG+cs.RO, 20pp, no journal ref. Every checkable element confirmed verbatim including the 32-step context / 64-step rollout protocol and the DreamerV3 baseline, and no code link exists on the abstract page or in the full text. CONFIDENCE IS LOW DESPITE THE UNANIMOUS VOTE, for four reasons. (1) DOMAIN: all DMC results use low-dimensional PROPRIOCEPTIVE state, the second domain is LiDAR vectors, the encoder 'applies a symlog transform to continuous vector inputs', and there are NO pixel/CNN/ViT observations anywhere — the paper's own abstract scopes it to 'proprioceptive continuous-control tasks'. So the result is unproven for a ViT-encoder visual latent like ours. (2) THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS SUSPECT AND THE AUTHORS SAY SO: 'Because separately learned latent coordinates are not directly comparable physical quantities, decoded observation error provides the stronger evidence' — Koopman's deterministic state is 2048-d vs DreamerV3's size12m preset, MSE appears raw and un-normalised in each model's OWN latent space, and a spectrally contractive latent has bounded norm BY CONSTRUCTION, so an unknown fraction of the 89.4 % may be a units artifact. Relay only the 23.2 % observation-space figure. (3) STATISTICS: seed count never stated, no confidence intervals, no significance tests, and one task (Walker Run) is WORSE on reward MSE at h=64 (1.2588 vs 1.1920). (4) The companion mechanism claim — the kappa*^H multiplicative bound making drift a tunable design knob — was voted down 0-3, as was the claim that its open-loop gain transferred to closed-loop UAV navigation (73.8 % vs 53.8 %); neither may be quoted. Verification was primary-source-only (search budget exhausted at 200/200), so no third-party critique or replication check exists.
findings.vote: 3-0 on the descriptive claim; 0-3 on both companion mechanism/closed-loop claims

findings.claim: RANK 9 (COVERAGE GAP — READ BEFORE ACTING ON ANY OTHER SECTION) — FOUR OF THE SIX REQUESTED AREAS PRODUCED ZERO SURVIVING EVIDENCE, SO NO RECOMMENDATION IS ADMISSIBLE IN THEM. Nothing survived verification on: (3) WORLD-ACTION MODELS / VLAs — no verified claim about pi-0 / pi-0.5, GR00T N1.x, RT-2 successors, OpenVLA, latent action models (LAPO, Genie-style latent actions), action tokenisation, action chunking, or flow-matching vs autoregressive action heads; (4) ROBOTICS — nothing on cross-embodiment transfer, Open-X/DROID-scale data beyond V-JEPA 2-AC's 62-hour slice, sim-to-real, hierarchical high-level-reasoner-plus-low-level-controller policies, or failure recovery; (5) LLMs — nothing on reasoning / test-time compute, distillation into small models, hierarchical or multi-agent controllers, or structured latent reasoning for a strategic planner; (6) FOUNDATION MODELS — nothing on scaling laws for small models, data quality vs quantity, curriculum, mixture-of-experts at small scale, or efficient pretraining. Also absent: Genie 3, DreamerV4, and the Cosmos world foundation models, none of which appear in any surviving claim. DIRECT CONSEQUENCES FOR OUR OPEN QUESTIONS: (a) our anchor-count-over-encoder-scale knee (54.7M / 104.2M / 251.9M at identical corpus and steps) and our inverse-small-is-better IDM result (0.86M > 2.90M > 19.98M) receive NEITHER support nor challenge — the small-model scaling-law literature was not successfully verified at all; (b) our oracle target-speed lever (88.7 % of the goal-conditioning gap, head R2 0.7635 but RMSE 4.4545 m/s) receives no external guidance; (c) MOST IMPORTANTLY, requirement (c) of the brief — giving a small model a strategic/topological prior WITHOUT map labels, which our PhysicalAI-AV corpus makes mandatory since it has no map, lane graph, junction annotation, route/goal signal or GNSS — has ZERO verified evidence. The only candidate, an action-free latent sub-goal planner trained purely on latent embeddings of successful demonstrations (FF-JEPA, arXiv 2606.09311), was refuted 0-3 on all three of its claims and must be treated as an UNVERIFIED LEAD, not as a design input. Recommended action: a dedicated second research pass scoped to (3)-(6) plus the no-map strategic prior, with a search budget that is not exhausted on the horizon question.
findings.evidence: This is a verified fact about the composition of THIS evidence set, not an external claim: of the seven claims that survived three-vote adversarial verification, all seven concern the JEPA family and world-model rollout horizon; the eighteen refuted claims cluster on frozen-vs-trained encoders (7), FF-JEPA long-horizon decomposition (3), MoP-JEPA planning metrics (2), JEPA collapse controls from Sub-JEPA arXiv 2605.09241 (2, both split 1-2) and Delta-JEPA arXiv 2606.31232 (3, votes 1-2/0-3/0-3), SkyJEPA's physics-structured decoder (1), HorizonDrive's Scheduled Rollout Recovery result (1) and Koopman's bound and closed-loop transfer (2). Two collapse-control leads worth re-probing but NOT quotable: Sub-JEPA's proposal to impose an isotropic Gaussian prior inside multiple random LOW-DIMENSIONAL SUBSPACES rather than the full ambient embedding (1-2, has public code, low-dimensional control only), which is a cheap regulariser swap against our existing SIGReg term (SigRegConfig in stack/tanitad/config.py, n_slices=512, weight 0.1, free_dims exemption); and Delta-JEPA's proposal that an inverse-dynamics decoder should take the latent DISPLACEMENT z_{t+1}−z_t rather than concatenated endpoints (1-2, reported +12.60 points on Push-T), which is a one-line change to our IDM and bears on our small-IDM-is-better result by asserting that decoder INPUT FORM, not capacity, is the lever. Both split 1-2 — evidence class HYPOTHESIS, admissible for experiment design, not for a decision. Note also a methodological limitation of the pass itself: at least three verifiers reported exhausting a 200/200 WebSearch budget, which is a plausible partial explanation for the coverage gap and is a reason to re-probe rather than to conclude these areas are empty (our own absence-found-at-one-location-is-not-absence rule applies to this very finding).
findings.vote: n/a — composition of the verified set (7 surviving, 18 refuted)

result.caveats:
EVIDENCE CLASS. Under CLAUDE.md rule 1 every external number in this report is PUBLISHED, never MEASURED. One surviving claim self-labelled a third-party arXiv latency figure "MEASURED design claim" — a category error, relabelled here. The only MEASURED-ours items are the code facts I read this session in stack/tanitad/models/predictor.py (fixed window=6 with a learned per-position embedding and an asserted window match; horizons default (1,2,4); `self.out_proj = nn.Linear(state_dim, d)  # reserved: feed predictions back`, i.e. the autoregressive feedback path is declared but unwired), stack/tanitad/config.py:50-58, and stack/tanitad/models/flagship_v4.py:72-73 (DENSE_HORIZONS 1..20 = 2 s dense, TACTICAL_HORIZONS 5..50 = 5 s coarse — the cap is on the dense/operative path).

SOURCE QUALITY. Only ONE of the five sources is a major-lab technical report with released weights and real-hardware results (V-JEPA 2, Meta FAIR). The other four are unrefereed arXiv preprints; SkyJEPA and HorizonDrive are marked "Under Review", Koopman Dreamer was 7 days old at verification and MoP-JEPA 3 weeks. NONE has been independently replicated, and no third-party critique was obtainable for SkyJEPA, HorizonDrive's architecture claim, or Koopman because at least three verifiers hit a 200/200 WebSearch budget ceiling and could only verify primary-source-only. The research question's "benchmarks with public reproducible numbers" bar is therefore NOT met by four of five sources: no code repository was found for SkyJEPA or Koopman Dreamer, and HorizonDrive's code availability is UNCONFIRMED (one verifier cited github.com/zcliangyue/HorizonDrive inside a claim that was itself refuted 0-3; another found none).

CORRECTIONS APPLIED DURING SYNTHESIS. (1) MoP-JEPA's distance-14 baselines are Dense (single-output) and MDN, NOT "codebook" — the codebook control belongs to a different experiment (coverage of stochastic dynamics) as a context-free baseline. The correction strengthens the result, since MDN is the stronger competitor. (2) HorizonDrive "stable to 20 s" softened to "quantitatively evaluated to ~20 s, degrading more slowly than the strongest streaming baselines" — its own Appendix D is an error-accumulation analysis, so error still grows inside the 20 s. (3) SkyJEPA's "bounded compounding ratio" softened: CR is still RISING at k=60, not asymptoting. (4) Koopman's 89.4 % demoted to suggestive-only in favour of the 23.2 % observation-space figure, per the authors' own statement that separately learned latent coordinates are not comparable quantities and because a spectrally contractive latent has bounded norm by construction.

TRANSFER-GAP RISK — THE BIGGEST WEAKNESS OF THIS EVIDENCE SET. Not one source measures what we measure. V-JEPA 2-AC is tabletop manipulation at 4 fps and 16 s/action with human-provided sub-goals and a hand-tuned camera; MoP-JEPA is 2-D pointmaze graph search over real dataset states; SkyJEPA is quadrotor state prediction over a low-dimensional physics vector with a physics-structured prober; Koopman Dreamer is proprioceptive DMC and LiDAR vectors with no pixel results at all; HorizonDrive is a pixel-reconstructive video-VAE latent scored with FID/FVD. NONE reports metric ADE from a high-dimensional visual predictive latent on a driving corpus. What transfers is MECHANISM and INSTRUMENTATION (CR_k/ER_k, rolling-window recursion, rollout-recovery training, spectral constraint); the NUMBERS do not, and quoting 1.4-at-3x or 89.4 % as if they applied to a 286.3M vision model would repeat exactly the prose-copying failure mode CLAUDE.md was written to stop.

TIME SENSITIVITY. Four of five sources are 10 weeks old or less and three are under review, so any could change materially on peer review. A V-JEPA 2.1 exists (HF hosting request Mar 2026) but supersedes the PRETRAINING checkpoints, not the 2-AC robot measurements; V-JEPA 2's arXiv entry still shows [v1] only with no erratum. One verifier could not complete a second probe for a V-JEPA 3, so "no successor flagship" is UNCONFIRMED, not established. Unverified 2026 leads (FF-JEPA 2606.09311, ThinkJEPA 2603.22281, VLA-JEPA at ECCV 2026, MoP-JEPA's siblings) suggest the field is trending toward HIERARCHICAL SUB-GOAL DECOMPOSITION rather than longer single rollouts — which would map directly onto our strategic/tactical/operative split — but none was verifiable in this pass and none may be cited. The safe conclusion is narrow: our 2 s cap is not obviously behind V-JEPA 2; it IS behind HorizonDrive's ~20 s driving-specific quantitative horizon; and it is untested against the 2026 hierarchical-planner literature.

ASYMMETRY OF THE REFUTED SET. Eighteen claims were refuted, seven of them on frozen-vs-trained encoders and in BOTH directions — the strongest apparent contradiction of our result AND the three strongest apparent corroborations all failed. Treat this as an evidentiary vacuum, not as vindication: absence of a verified contradiction is not corroboration, and our own MEASURED numbers remain the only admissible evidence on that question.
openQuestions: Does our pure-imagination decay actually COMPOUND, or is it task difficulty? Nothing in the literature answers this for us — CR_k = e_rollout/e_teacher-forced at k=4/8/16/20 on the deployed arm is unknown until we run it, and the answer decides whether the 1.03 -> 1.91 exponent justifies any architecture change at all. If CR_k comes back near 1, our most-quoted imagination result needs a retraction entry under the 'interpretation not re-derived from the instrument' root-cause class.

Is there ANY verified method to give a sub-300M model a strategic/topological prior WITHOUT map labels? This was requirement (c) of the brief and it received zero surviving evidence. The obvious lead — an action-free latent sub-goal planner distilling the topology from the demonstration distribution itself rather than from annotations (FF-JEPA, arXiv 2606.09311) — was refuted 0-3 on all three of its claims within this pass. Is that paper real and does it hold, and if not, does the alternative reduce to importing a lane graph from a simulator or an external corpus, given PhysicalAI-AV has no map, no route signal and clip-local metres only (no GNSS, so OSM map-matching is impossible)?

Does the frozen-encoder ceiling depend on IMAGE- versus VIDEO-pretraining? Our 2.92 m speed-blind ceiling was measured with DINOv2 and I-JEPA, both image-pretrained; V-JEPA 2-AC's working frozen encoder was motion-supervised on 1M+ hours of video. Nobody has run frozen-video-encoder versus from-scratch on a metric driving task. Secondary and possibly decisive: even a positive result is undeployable at ViT-g scale (1B params, 3.5x our entire budget), so does a distillation path exist that preserves whatever the video pretraining buys?

Does rollout-recovery training (HorizonDrive's Scheduled Rollout Recovery: sample training contexts from the model's own rollout trajectory) transfer from a pixel-RECONSTRUCTIVE VAE latent to a JEPA-style PREDICTIVE latent? In HorizonDrive a decoder anchors the latent to pixels, so corrupted-context training cannot collapse the representation. We have no decoder — the same procedure could instead teach the encoder to ignore its input, and its interaction with our existing SIGReg anti-collapse term (n_slices=512, weight 0.1, free_dims exemption in stack/tanitad/config.py) is completely unmeasured. A collapse monitor would have to be part of any such run.

refuted.claim: The video encoder is explicitly FROZEN during action-conditioned post-training — only the predictor is learned on top of a 1B-parameter ViT-g pretrained on internet video. This is the strongest 2025-26 counter-evidence to our measured frozen-encoder ceiling (DINOv2 / I-JEPA at 2.92 m fwd ADE, speed-blind, fixed to 0.83 m by a from-scratch encoder with speed as an action channel). IMPORTANT QUALIFIER before treating it as a contradiction: the task is tabletop manipulation with image goals and relative end-effector actions at 16 s/action, not metric longitudinal prediction at road speed; and the frozen encoder here was pretrained on 1M+ hours of VIDEO (motion-supervised), unlike DINOv2's image pretraining. The discriminating experiment for us is a frozen V-JEPA 2 encoder (video-pretrained, not image-pretrained) against our from-scratch ViT on the same corpus and steps.

A FLAT (single-level) latent world model collapses catastrophically when the planning horizon is extended, while a hierarchical subgoal decomposition over the SAME world model does not: on PushT, flat LeWM scores 94.53% success at 25 steps but only 3.52% at 75 steps and 0.00% under random initialization, whereas hierarchical FF-JEPA (diffusion planner) holds 96.09% / 91.80% / 82.42% on the same three conditions. This is the same failure mode as TanitAD's accelerating pure-imagination decay (local exponent 1.03 -> 1.91 over 0.4-2.0s) and it argues the fix is architectural decomposition into chained short rollouts, not a longer single rollout or a bigger horizon embedding.

Long-horizon latent planning can be achieved WITHOUT any explicit goal image, map, or goal annotation: an ACTION-FREE latent planner trained only on latent embeddings of successful demonstrations predicts the next subgoal, replacing the goal-state input that every compared baseline requires. This is a directly transferable formulation for a strategic brain on a corpus (PhysicalAI-AV) that has no map, lane graph, route or GNSS signal — the topological/goal prior is distilled from the demonstration distribution itself rather than from labels.

A small task-trained latent world-model encoder (LeWM, 18M params) beats a FROZEN generic DINOv2 encoder (DINO-WM) at long horizon under an otherwise matched hierarchical planner: 91.80% vs 61.0% success at the long horizon, while being merely competitive at short horizon (96.09% vs 89.0%). The frozen-generic-encoder penalty therefore GROWS with rollout length — consistent with, and an independent replication of, TanitAD's measured frozen-encoder ceiling (DINOv2/I-JEPA 2.92m fwd ADE, speed-blind) rather than a contradiction of it.

Pixel-reconstruction fidelity and action-relevance of a latent space are orthogonal on LIBERO: at PSNR ~20 dB frozen inverse-dynamics action R2 spans -0.01 to +0.46, and the two highest-PSNR encoders (SDXL VAE, Cosmos-1 tokenizer) attain the LOWEST action R2 (-0.55 and -0.36 frozen; -0.41 and -0.29 even after inverse-dynamics fine-tuning). Protocol: 8 encoder families, fixed MLP probe [D->256->128->7], LIBERO task-OOD split (104 train / 26 held-out tasks), 3 probe seeds, 17M ConvTranspose decoder to put encoder-only backbones on a common PSNR axis. Directly supports TanitAD's latent-not-pixel design intent and predicts that PSNR/FVD/LPIPS would be a misleading selection criterion for our transition predictor.

Image-only self-supervised encoders (Web-DINO ViT-L, a web-scale DINOv2 successor; SigLIP 2 ViT-L) have a REPRESENTATIONAL, not optimisation-level, ceiling on action recoverability: frozen action R2 is -0.01 / +0.05, and even with a full inverse-dynamics fine-tune they reach only 0.16-0.17, with a lambda sweep across five orders of magnitude confining them to a 0.1-wide R2 band. On MetaWorld both go negative. This is independent corroboration of TanitAD's measured frozen-DINOv2 driving ceiling (2.92 m fwd ADE, speed-blind) and falsifies 'a stronger head can repair a frozen generic image encoder'.

FROZEN pretrained encoders collapse catastrophically under mild visual corruption while the SAME backbone with a small inverse-dynamics auxiliary loss degrades gracefully: frozen V-JEPA 2 ViT-L goes 0.40 clean -> -4.66 under blur-11 and -1.18 under noise-0.15, frozen VideoMAE -> -2.54, frozen Web-DINO -> -4.19 worst-case; with ID supervision V-JEPA 2 ViT-L holds 0.85 -> 0.56 worst-case and V-JEPA+ID beats VideoMAE+ID at matched clean R2 under noise 0.15 (0.66 vs 0.11). Strong 2025-26 evidence AGAINST 'a frozen generic video encoder suffices for control', and a cheap transfer for us: add an inverse-dynamics auxiliary head to the TanitAD encoder and measure corruption-robustness of the 4-brain arm.

Sub-JEPA claims that JEPA world-model collapse is best prevented by imposing an isotropic Gaussian prior inside MULTIPLE RANDOM LOW-DIMENSIONAL SUBSPACES of the embedding, not in the full ambient embedding space, because latent representations lie on low-dimensional manifolds and a full-space Gaussian prior over-biases them. This is a directly falsifiable, cheap-to-test regularizer swap for our latent transition predictor: same anti-collapse effect, weaker global constraint. Evidence quality: PUBLISHED-but-preprint (arXiv cs.LG, not stated peer-reviewed), with public code, tested only on low-dimensional continuous control.

The paper's premise is that END-TO-END JEPA training (encoder trained jointly with the predictor, i.e. our from-scratch regime rather than a frozen DINOv2/I-JEPA encoder) is unstable by default and collapses to trivial solutions absent an explicit structural constraint on the latent. This does NOT contradict our measured frozen-encoder ceiling (2.92 m, speed-blind) — it names the specific failure mode the trained-encoder alternative must be defended against, and implies our latent needs a monitored anti-collapse term rather than a frozen backbone.

Delta-JEPA's core architectural claim is that an inverse-dynamics action decoder should take the latent DISPLACEMENT (Δz_t = z_{t+1} − z_t) as input rather than the concatenation of the two endpoint embeddings; the ablation reports this change improves planning success on all four tasks, largest on Push-T (+12.60 points) and Two-Room (+4.07 points). This is a one-line, directly testable change to our own inverse-dynamics head (which currently uses concatenated endpoints), and bears on our measured result that a SMALLER IDM (0.86M > 2.90M > 19.98M) works better — the paper's mechanism says decoder INPUT FORM, not capacity, is the lever.

The paper asserts a specific, falsifiable collapse-control mechanism for JEPA-family latent world models: reconstruction-free joint-embedding objectives can collapse to ACTION-INSENSITIVE representations, and displacement-level action supervision prevents this because adjacent embeddings cannot collapse without destroying the action information needed to reconstruct the action. Crucially it claims this is achieved with NO pixel reconstruction and NO distribution-matching (VICReg/contrastive-style) regularizers — i.e. a collapse control compatible with our latent-space-only design intent.

The visual encoder is a RANDOMLY INITIALIZED (from-scratch) ViT-Tiny with a 6-layer causal Transformer dynamics predictor — i.e. a June-2026 JEPA-family world model designed for control deliberately does NOT use a frozen pretrained encoder. This is a same-side data point for our measured frozen-encoder ceiling (DINOv2/I-JEPA 2.92 m, speed-blind; from-scratch + speed channel 3.73 → 0.83 m), though it is weaker evidence than ours: the paper does not run a frozen-vs-trained ablation, so it shows a design choice, not a measured contradiction of the frozen-encoder position.

Under stochastic transitions, a single-regressor JEPA predictor is near-useless for graph-based planning: on held-out OGBench transitions, graph search built on single-output (dense L2/cosine) predictors succeeds on only 0.02-0.09 of queries, while a K-head hard-assigned mixture reaches 0.85 (per-maze planAll: med-stitch 0.851+/-0.08, teleport 0.748+/-0.09, large-stitch 0.386+/-0.45 vs dense 0.084/0.037/0.016). The stated mechanism is that squared/cosine regression returns the conditional mean, which under branching may correspond to no physically valid successor.

Raw coverage of successor states is a misleading metric for latent world models: a Mixture Density Network baseline attains high raw coverage while emitting many transitions that do not exist in the environment. Under the authors' verified-route metric (checks after graph construction that a path of REAL transitions exists), MoP-JEPA scores 0.247/0.192/0.139 vs MDN 0.134/0.039/0.057 across the three mazes, with transition precision 0.42-0.56 vs MDN 0.14-0.21.

The single largest driver of long-horizon accuracy is not the latent dynamics but the DECODER: mapping frozen latents to state through a physics-structured kinematic integrator (nominal quadrotor kinematics + learned residual corrections, integrated with the SO(3) exponential map) cuts 1-second open-loop position RMSE from 5.56 m to 1.43 m (3.9x) and attitude error from 40.20 deg to 4.71 deg (8.5x) versus an unstructured latent-to-state map. Structure in the readout, not more capacity, buys the horizon.

Training a driving world model to recover from its OWN prediction-corrupted histories (Scheduled Rollout Recovery) removes monotone error accumulation across a 19-chunk autoregressive rollout on nuScenes, whereas the self-forcing baseline (Self-Forcing++) degrades monotonically over the same horizon. Evidence quality: MEASURED by the authors, arXiv preprint (2605.11596v2, cs.CV), NOT peer-reviewed, but with public code (github.com/zcliangyue/HorizonDrive) and standard nuScenes metrics (FID 13.82 vs 28.84, FVD 92.99 vs 147.57, ARE 2.60 vs 3.78, DTW 3.27 vs 3.61). Directly targets our accelerating-decay problem (local exponent 1.03 -> 1.91 over 0.4-2.0s): the proposed mechanism is a TRAINING-TIME fix (sample contexts from the model's own rollout trajectory), not an architectural one, so it is cheap to test on our stack.

The paper derives a multi-step rollout-error bound that separates MULTIPLICATIVE amplification (governed by the spectral radius and the bilinear action Lipschitz constant, combined into kappa*, compounding as kappa*^H over H steps) from ADDITIVE stochastic-mismatch and residual terms — making long-horizon latent drift an explicit, tunable design knob rather than an emergent property, with a stated trade-off: lowering the radius attenuates error but erases persistent task information. This is the mechanism-level claim most relevant to our measured accelerating imagination decay (local exponent 1.03 -> 1.91 over 0.4-2.0s) and predicts that a super-unit effective spectral radius, not architecture depth, is the driver of the acceleration.

Improved open-loop imagination fidelity translated into improved CLOSED-LOOP control in the same system: on UAV-LiDAR autonomous navigation Koopman Dreamer reached 73.8% success / 26.2% failure versus 53.8% / 46.2% for DreamerV3 — a +20.0 percentage-point absolute gain. This is direct evidence against the assumption that open-loop rollout accuracy does not predict closed-loop performance, and bears on our measured open-loop-to-closed-loop gap (0.45m open-loop ADE -> 1.69m closed-loop). Caveat: single domain, single-paper result, no confidence intervals or seed counts quoted in the reported sentence.
